name: Drain
label: Revelation
lede: Drain began as UC Santa Cruz students trying every style at once and turned into a thrash-crossover band in board shorts. Revelation put out the debut just as touring stopped, a San Jose parking-lot show in June 2021 drew 2,000 people and helped start a hardcore boom, and Epitaph came next.

eras.title: College kids turn into a fight band
eras.text: Drain started with drummer Tim Flegal and a handful of UC Santa Cruz students trying whatever styles they liked. When that line-up fell apart, Sammy Ciaramitaro and Cody Chavez steered it toward hardcore, with a lot of 1980s thrash in the riffs.

years.h: Tim Flegal starts a band at UC Santa Cruz
years.p: The first Drain line-up is Flegal on drums with Aric Gibson, Patrick Delaney and Josh Nunes, all students, playing a mix of styles. It's gone by 2015.

years.src: Wikipedia: Drain · Kerrang! · BrooklynVegan: Drain talk
years.h: Two new members, and Drain stops dabbling
years.p: Singer Sammy Ciaramitaro and bassist Cody Chavez arrive as the first line-up breaks up, and the sound turns to hardcore. Demo '15 and Swan Songs follow.
years.xp:
Ciaramitaro grew up in an upper-middle-class Los Angeles suburb on gateway bands like [[The Offspring|23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067]] before hardcore's storytelling pulled him in. He also drums in San Jose's Gulch, which he co-founded.

Chavez soon moved from bass to guitar, and Justin Rhode took over bass in 2016.

years.h: Over Thinking comes out the year the singer gets sober
years.p: Justin Rhode is now on bass. Ciaramitaro told Stereogum he got sober in 2016.
years.xp: Stereogum's interview describes him taking pride in writing about abstinence from angles beyond the usual straight-edge pitch.

years.h: A Twilight Zone title for the second EP
years.p: Time Enough at Last is named for the Twilight Zone episode about a bookworm.

eras.title: A debut into lockdown, then a parking lot
eras.text: One set at Sound and Fury got Drain onto Revelation, and California Cursed came out in April 2020, weeks into the pandemic. When shows came back, Drain and their friends didn't wait for promoters.

years.h: One Sound and Fury set gets Drain signed to Revelation
years.p: Revelation Records sees the band at the 2019 festival and signs them.
Ten songs in 22 minutes, first teased with Sick One in February. Every planned tour date goes with the spring.
years.xp:
Ciaramitaro, Chavez, Justin Rhode and Flegal wrote it together and recorded it through 2019. It opens with Feel the Pressure, and Kerrang! says it's about self-worth and the displacement tech-industry gentrification brought to the Bay Area.

Exclaim!'s Conor Atkinson gave it 8/10 and said it had the "power to transport your mind out of the dystopian nightmare we are all navigating." Stereogum's Tom Breihan called it old-school California fight music with a generous whiff of '80s thrash.

years.h: Bassist Justin Rhode out, Mike "Durt" Durrett in
years.p: Rhode played on California Cursed. Durrett holds the bass until 2022, and on Living Proof guitarist Cody Chavez plays bass too.

years.h: A girlfriend falls through the ceiling, and a landlord goes to war
years.p: Stereogum reported that Ciaramitaro's girlfriend fell 15 feet through their rental's ceiling and broke her foot. Four months of the landlord leaving razors and glass outside and forging evidence followed.
years.xp: Ciaramitaro's own summary to Stereogum of those four months: "mental fucking warfare." He describes himself as a pessimist by default, which sits oddly with a reputation as the nicest person in the scene.

q: We realized we could do this ourselves, that we don't need anybody else.
yt: Drain's full set, San Jose, June 19, 2021
years.h: Gulch and Drain throw their own show in a San Jose parking lot
years.p: About 2,000 people pay $5 for Drain, Gulch, [[Scowl|c81f7820-ee5b-46ef-9b78-027d38b9a1aa]], [[Sunami|1b53aa11-ccef-457f-90d9-5165b270fdc5]], Xibalba and Maya Over Eyes, with no promoter involved. Some fly in.
years.xp:
The bands printed the merch and built the stage themselves. Stereogum later wrote that the show kicked off the national hardcore renaissance by accident, and the New York Times called Drain a driving force of it.

The night went by the name Real Bay Shit.

eras.title: Epitaph, and a borrowed cymbal
eras.text: Epitaph signed Drain on the understanding that California Cursed would get its tour first. Living Proof, cut partly at Dave Grohl's Studio 606, ended on a clean-sung Descendents cover and topped Revolver's hardcore list.

yt: Feel the Pressure, Audiotree Live, late 2022
years.h: Drain leave Revelation for Epitaph, but tour first
years.p: After six to eight months of negotiating, Epitaph Records agrees to let the band tour California Cursed properly before any new record. Watch You Burn is the first Epitaph single.
years.xp: Ciaramitaro called Watch You Burn a "pissed off and in your face song that I wrote after hitting a breaking point this year."

years.cap: Tim Flegal behind the kit at Pol'and'Rock festival, Poland, August 2023
years.src: Stereogum · Wikipedia: Living Proof · BrooklynVegan: Drain talk
years.h: Flegal breaks a cymbal at Studio 606 and plays Taylor Hawkins's instead
years.p: Drain were cutting Living Proof weeks after the Foo Fighters drummer died. Ten songs in 25 minutes, out May 5 on Epitaph.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Studio 606 and The Pit, and closes out with a clean-sung cover of [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]]' Good Good Things. Track six is a rap interlude, and the Grateful Dead nods run throughout.

Kerrang!'s Luke Morton gave it 5/5, Exclaim!'s Paul Dika 9/10 and Clash 8/10. Ciaramitaro told Stereogum he reads the Descendents song as a conversation about trust between partners.

On the lyrics, he said they are "just one of those things I think a lot of fans skip over."

years.cap: Drain's set at Pol'and'Rock festival, Poland, August 2023
yt: A day on tour, The Warfield, San Francisco, April 2024
years.h: A headline run across the US, then Europe for most of August
years.p: [[Drug Church|32d2897c-4c91-46db-8161-f51d3f4f0d93]], Gel and Magnitude rotate as support in the US, then Drain play Europe August 3-19, including Poland's Pol'and'Rock festival. Earlier in 2023 they toured Australia with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]].

years.cap: Drain at Pol'and'Rock festival, Poland, August 2023
years.h: Revolver puts Living Proof at the top of 2023's hardcore albums
years.p: Stereogum ranks it 47th among all albums that year and eighth among hardcore ones.
years.xp: Loudwire put it among the year's 25 best rock and metal albums, and BrooklynVegan had it in its mid-year hardcore top 10.

eras.title: Drain is your friend
eras.text: By their third album Drain were on Warped Tour and metal festival bills, with Ciaramitaro still working the merch table himself. The record was cut live to catch what they sound like in a room.

years.big: "I got to do all of those things with my best friends."
years.h: Third album announced, and Nights Like These is the first single
years.p: Ciaramitaro, in the announcement, on how the band's run feels. Derek Rathbun directs the video, which has the band playing as they are now and as imagined old men.
years.xp: Ciaramitaro said of the old-age makeup: "I am going to look just like my dad when I get old - I should just use him."

years.h: Drain take the revived Warped Tour, then the metal festivals
years.p: After Warped Tour come Inkcarceration in Ohio, Louder Than Life in Louisville, New England Metal & Hardcore Festival and Furnace Fest in Alabama.

years.cap: Sammy Ciaramitaro at Pol'and'Rock festival, Poland, August 2023
q: I want to be the face everyone says hello to.
years.h: Drain cut ...Is Your Friend live, with Jon Markson · Epitaph
years.p: Markson, who has produced The Story So Far and Drug Church, records the whole album live to keep the band's stage energy.
years.xp: Ciaramitaro still works the merch table at every show; he told Kerrang! he wants to be the face everyone says hello to. Off the road he's worked at Printhead, a San Jose T-shirt shop run by his former bandmate Cole Kakimoto.

years.h: Greg Cerwonka goes from touring bassist to full member
years.p: He follows Sam Jameson (2023–25) on bass. Through every bass change, Flegal, Ciaramitaro and Chavez haven't moved.
